lines.text: Nedamex is an evidence graph for rare diseases: over thirty diseases and thousands of sourced links.
Nine AI coding agents built it in parallel — each on its own branch, coordinated through one shared log, plus a tester agent that behaves like a real user.
The data comes from public sources — Orphanet, HPO, ClinVar, PubMed, ClinicalTrials.gov, Open Targets, NIH RePORTER, openFDA and EMA — stored in Supabase.
OpenAI's gpt-4o-mini extracts and explains, but a verifier deletes any sentence without a citation. ElevenLabs gives every guide its own voice.
Next.js on Vercel runs the engine, Lovable hosts the platform, and Blender and Remotion made the 3D and this video.
What worked: one shared log, strict ownership of files, and a tester that caught wrong 'approved' labels before anyone else did.
What didn't: our cloud sandbox couldn't reach the APIs, the first graph shook, and a rename mid-build touched every screen.
